cells.tense: You are carrying several true readings of one thing, and your hands are steady.
cells.act: declare the shape of it outward, plainly
cells.ask: At a table with people who matter, name the shape of a shared situation once — what you see it to be — and then let the talking go where it goes.
cells.core: In this room, when a pattern comes clear, you can hold several readings of the same thing at once and not rush a verdict. People bring you a tangle and you see where the lines run, often before they've finished talking. That isn't coldness. It's the whole pattern finding somewhere to land. What's missing is that some of it gets said. You can sit quiet with a dozen readings and be right, and the person across from you is still waiting for one plain sentence. This week, hand one over — say the shape as you see it, once, without arguing your case. Let them decide what to do with it. What was held whole inside you becomes something two people can pick up.
cells.sheetLine: Seeing it whole isn't the same as having said it.
cells.verb: holding many readings of a thing at once
cells.place: where the whole pattern shows itself to you

cells.tense: The readings keep multiplying, and you are combing every branch before anything gets chosen.
cells.act: turn toward the one direction and stop surveying
cells.ask: Follow one reading you're carrying for three days — act as though it were the whole truth, and leave the other versions where they are.
cells.core: Where the whole pattern shows itself, the readings have kept multiplying. Every angle has a version, every version stays live, and you keep adding views instead of setting one down and moving. Held this wide, seeing more stops being sight and becomes a way to avoid a choice. A mind can hold many truths and still only walk one direction. So for three days, take one of them as what's true and act from it — not the safest one, the one you'd steer by if it came to that. The rest can wait; they'll keep. Purpose that doesn't land in a heading isn't a stance, it's the broadest way of standing still.
cells.sheetLine: Seeing every branch isn't the same as moving on one.

cells.tense: The pattern does not come together, because nothing here is left to build it from.
cells.act: let the vision be shared with one other
cells.ask: Take a puzzle you keep turning over to someone you trust and say the pieces out loud — no finished pattern needed, just the parts.
cells.core: Where the pattern used to show itself, the pieces arrive and nothing holds them together. You get more of what's true and less of what it's true about, and lately you'd rather keep quiet than say any of it half-formed. That's the tired part talking. Seeing whole isn't done alone; it happens when what's in your head meets someone else's and the two of you turn it over. So bring a puzzle you keep worrying to a person you trust — not to be handed the answer, just to say it. Their view is one more piece, not a verdict. Do that once this week, whatever shape the conversation ends up taking.
cells.sheetLine: Nothing becomes a pattern while it's sitting in one head.

cells.tense: You read the whole thing correctly and file it under something other than your own name.
cells.act: do the fair thing where no one will see
cells.ask: Before sleep, recall one quiet call you made this week — you saw how something stood and acted on it — and count that as yours.
cells.core: You can see how a thing really stands, across the layers, and then act from it — and your own account leaves that out. 'It was obvious.' 'Anyone would have.' So the calls get made and the credit goes to circumstance, and you get practice at not being the one who decided. The record of you, kept elsewhere, has you in it. This week, take a small case where you saw the truth of it and did the right thing — nothing anyone applauded — and mark it as yours, in your own head, before you sleep. Your read stands whether or not anyone agrees with it. What's off isn't your sight. It's that you've stopped signing it.
cells.sheetLine: You keep reading it right and filing it under circumstance.
